task.title: Refuse newer-writer packs with an upgrade signal instead of corrupt-data
task.description:
From v0.5.0 on, readers should distinguish 'this history was written by a newer workbook' from 'this history is corrupt.' Today any pack using semantics an older build cannot fold is reported as corrupt-data (measured on v0.4.4: a custom-status pack blocks the ref at fetch time forever; a restore-into pack reads fine but fails validate permanently, per the PR #95 review record). Installed binaries are frozen, but v0.5.0 is unreleased — teaching it the signal now makes this the last hard edge.

Design direction (agreed 2026-08-13): operation packs (task and config ledger) carry a writer-format marker ONLY when they use semantics older readers cannot fold — a minimum-reader version, bumped deliberately per breaking change; its absence means 'foldable by v0.5.0', so no pack any current build writes changes by a byte (byte-compat golden required). A reader encountering a marker above its own version — including an unrecognized operation type under such a marker — refuses with a distinct category and a message telling the user to upgrade workbook, scoped like today's refusals (per task / per ledger), never wedging sync or holding back other refs; validate reports the same way.

First consumer: the comments/attachments story (WB-01KYD77EV9XVA1K0KBY2561GGC) ships new operation types that must carry the marker; that story depends on this one.

## Shipped (2026-08-13, PR #97)

One PR through a two-round adversarial execution-verified review (record on the PR).

The marker is `minReader`, an optional integer format generation on operation packs AND checkpoints — checkpoints carry a running watermark (max over history), which the review proved load-bearing against a real mixed history: a gen-1 pack buried under later gen-0 packs still refuses on the old side where a tip-only check would fold it. Writers declare the generation per operation type (core.operationMinReader / configOperationMinReader, every entry 0 today — the table the comments/attachments and assignments stories bump); PackMinReader derives a pack's marker in NewOperationPack, the single author of the durable header. The marker is consulted only after a strict decode fails; a document that does not parse cannot claim one, so corruption stays reachable. New category `newer-writer`, exit 9; validate deliberately fails on a history it could not audit; corruption reported first. Reads on an old build serve from checkpoints with a non-fatal advisory; mutations refuse with the upgrade message; fetch/sync/push advance and never wedge; divergence replay refuses while changing nothing (nothing parked, local ops intact, task withheld from push — and the config ledger takes the identical path via a skip inside publishConfigLedger, so its five call sites cannot disagree). Projection schema 3 stores the watermark and per-pack generations.

Round-1 gates, all fixed and re-verified: the validation cache carried a newer-writer verdict across the upgrade that answers it (fixed by recording the reader generation in cache metadata — chosen over never-caching because a `valid` verdict from a NEWER build is equally uninheritable by an older one; the coupling requirement now lives beside SupportedFormatGeneration and binds future caches); the config ledger was not withheld from push (the doubled network-flavored refusal the task path was designed to avoid); the projection watermark restore had zero coverage despite being proven load-bearing by a mutant binary (a mutation could silently write a gen-0 checkpoint onto a gen-1 history — now pinned exactly).

Byte-compat was verified independently in BOTH rounds: main-built vs PR-built binaries over the full verb sequence, all 53 written documents byte-identical modulo ULIDs/wall-times, the marker appearing in no current write and the cache metadata key in no git-stored document.

**Contract for the stories that bump the generation:** add the op type's entry to the minReader table, bump SupportedFormatGeneration, and the reader-generation cache metadata triggers the one full revalidation automatically — see the COUPLING paragraph beside the constant. Recorded residual: a standalone `workbook push` in a fresh process still surfaces a git-flavored rejection for newer-generation refs (pre-existing standalone-push semantics; nothing lost; the softer message is scoped to the run that already reported the refusal).
